item.description:
Footnotes in the margin, embeds you can see, and pull quotes.

  • Footnotes in saved articles sit in the margin beside the line that cites them, and ink in word by word as you reach them. Click a number to find its note.
  • Prefer a clear margin? Settings ▸ Reading ▸ Footnotes in the margin, off, keeps them at the end of the piece and shows each one when you hover its number. On narrow windows they always work this way.
  • Embedded posts, videos and podcasts (X, Bluesky, YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Substack and more) show as a quiet row that links to the original, instead of vanishing.
  • Pull quotes, the enlarged lines magazines set between paragraphs, now keep their emphasis in the reader. This works for Aeon, Substack, WordPress sites and others that mark them up.
  • Typed section breaks like * * * or ⁂ appear as the reader’s own section break.
  • An article’s subtitle, when the page has one, sits under its title in the reader.
  • The reader’s top bar no longer repeats the percentage read; the margin shows it.
  • All of this applies to articles saved from now on.

Lots of small things: more in Settings, smarter saving, and Aa settings for one piece.

  • Aa can change just the piece you’re reading: choose This piece at the top. Make these my defaults hands them to every piece.
  • The colophon shows how long you’ve spent reading a piece, counted while you’re actually reading it.
  • Look up details in the colophon asks Open Library for a book’s missing author, year, publisher and language.
  • Under Today’s greeting, a line about the day: your stack, today’s arrivals, or how far you are through a book.
  • Settings ▸ Reading: a default paper, margin notes on or off, opening articles and PDFs at the top, and when a piece counts as finished.
  • Settings ▸ Today: deal 3, 4 or 5 cards from the backlog, and choose which sections sit beside the stack.
  • Settings ▸ Saving: whether new pieces go on the stack, category suggestions, keeping or skipping duplicates, and importing a reading list from Pocket, Instapaper or a file of links.
  • Settings ▸ Library: how long the bin keeps deleted pieces, a weekly backup of the database, and your whole library as JSON.
  • Settings ▸ Appearance & motion: evening colours on a schedule, and tilting covers on or off.
  • Saving shows how far each piece has got, such as images 3 of 11 or chapter 12 of 49, and warns about paywalled pages, with Save anyway.
  • Save can put everything in one category, and shows the title of a pasted link before you save it.
  • Exporting highlights to Markdown works again. It had been quietly failing to write the file.
  • Quotes saved before 2.4.0 lose their footnote numbers the next time you open their piece.
  • Delete a highlight from the Highlights tab with the bin that appears on hover, or by right-clicking it there or in Marginalia on Today.

Every piece gets a colophon.

  • The colophon replaces Details: a panel on the reader’s right edge, opened with the new “i” beside Aa or with ⌘I.
  • It has the piece’s cover and title (click to rename), then the work itself: author, year, publisher, ISBN, language and length, edited in place.
  • Below that, the piece in your library: category, kind and tags, when you saved it, how far you are, and how many highlights and notes it has. Then its file or original link.
  • New books bring their publisher, ISBN and language with them. PDFs named with their ISBN keep it, and articles keep their language.
  • Highlighting the start of an opening paragraph no longer shrinks its large first letter, and the selection now shows over it.
  • Highlights that end at the end of a paragraph, or run across two, are now tinted all the way through.
  • Quotes in Marginalia and Highlights leave out footnote markers: “Text¹ blah” is kept as “Text blah”.
  • “Put on the stack” in Save now decides for articles too. They used to go on the stack whatever it said.
